output.title: Chipboard panel cutting & preparation

product.name: Chipboard furniture panel
product.description: Rectangular chipboard furniture panel cut from raw sheets (up to 2.0 × 0.8 m), finished to 18 mm thickness. Edges are edge-banded, hinge/dowel holes are drilled, and panels are pallet-stacked for assembly.

steps.name: CutToSize
steps.does: Saw the chipboard panel to the required finished dimensions.

steps.name: ApplyEdgeBand
steps.does: Glue edge banding onto the visible edges of the cut panel.

steps.name: DrillHingeAndDowelHoles
steps.does: Drill hinge and dowel holes in the finished panel.

steps.name: InspectDimensions
steps.does: Operator checks panel dimensions periodically and identifies any out-of-tolerance parts.

steps.name: StackOnPallet
steps.does: Stack finished panels onto a pallet for downstream assembly.

output.quality: Operator dimension checks (periodic) find out-of-tolerance panels; those panels are set aside for rework or scrap (tolerance method and disposition not specified).
constraints: Dust extraction is required at the saw and drill operations.
assumptions: “About 90 panels per hour” is the required finished throughput (including cutting, edge banding, drilling, inspection, and pallet stacking).
Finished panels are rectangles with thickness 18 mm; plan dimensions are approximated to fit within the stated raw maximum size (2.0 × 0.8 m).
Edge banding includes gluing and pressing/holding long enough to bond, but exact press/curing time is not specified.
Inspection is periodic (not 100%) as stated; the actual sampling frequency and tolerance criteria are not specified.
Palletizing is handled manually or with a simple stacking assist; pallet size/count not specified.

questions.question: Does “90 panels per hour” mean finished, pallet-stacked panels leaving the line (after inspection), or cutting-only throughput?
questions.why: This sets whether the takt must accommodate all steps or only sawing, which can change the station time budgets.

questions.question: How are pallets handled at the end: manual placement, a pallet conveyor/feeder, or palletizing robot? What pallet dimensions and target stack height (or panels per pallet)?
questions.why: Determines the pallet stack station design and transport method.

questions.question: When a panel fails the dimension check, is it reworked (e.g., re-saw/edge re-trim), scrapped, or both? Also, what tolerance basis is used (e.g., gauge/vision, sampling rate)?
questions.why: Determines the reject path and whether an automated check station is needed or operator handling is sufficient.
